TEXT WITH PADA MARKERS

sarveṣāmapi muktyarthaṃ muktimārgasya darśanam 
deveśa jñānamācāraṃ kṛpayā kathayasva me // Dka_1

jñānācārau varārohe kathayāmi tavādhunā 
praviśanti yato mokṣaṃ jñānino dhvastakalmaṣam // Dka_2

yeṣāṃ bodhena saṃjātaṃ kālajñānaṃ varānane 
na teṣāṃ jāyate bodhaḥ śāstrakoṭiśatairapi // Dka_3

ato hi nirbhayo vidvān niḥśaṅko vigataspṛhaḥ 
jñānotsāhaparo bhūyāt śraddaddhāno nirākulaḥ // Dka_4

nirmamaḥ karuṇopetaḥ sarvabhūtābhayapradaḥ 
bhajet kālottaraṃ devi mumukṣuryogatatparaḥ // Dka_5

sa brahmā sa śivo viṣṇuḥ sa indraḥ sa ṣaḍānanaḥ 
sa guruḥ sarvadevāśca sa yogī sa tapodhanaḥ // Dka_6

paṇḍitaḥ sa mahābhāgaḥ kṛtārthaḥ paramārthataḥ 
caladvāyusamaṃ cittaṃ dhriyate yena niścalam // Dka_7

sa upāyo mimokṣasya sadupāttaguṇastu saḥ 
sā prajñā tadiha sthairyaṃ tatpuṇyaṃ vyavasāyinām // Dka_8

tadeva tīrthaṃ dānaṃ ca sa tapaśca na saṃśayaḥ 
yenopāyena badhyeta vāyubhiścalanaṃ manaḥ // Dka_9

citte calati saṃsāro niścalo mokṣa eva tu 
tasmāccittaṃ sthiraṃ kuryāt prajñayā parayā budhaḥ // Dka_10

ekāntikaṃ sukhaṃ yatra tathāivātyantikaṃ bhavet 
niṣkarmaṇi pare tattve ko na rajyeta paṇḍitaḥ // Dka_11

nivṛtto viṣayajñānāt niṣkalajñānatatparaḥ 
anicchannapi medhāvī labhate mokṣamakṣayam // Dka_12

asmitākalayā yuktaṃ caitanyaṃ sakalaṃ smṛtam 
asmitārahitaṃ cetaś caitanyaṃ śaktirucyate // Dka_13

tathā prakāśitaṃ viśvaṃ śaktidhyānamudāhṛtam 
sarvālambavinirmuktaṃ niṣkalaṃ jñānamucyate // Dka_14

ahamaṃśena yacchūnyaṃ cinmātrālokamadvayam 
muktibījaṃ tadākhyātaṃ parayogapravartakam // Dka_15

cakrāṇi nāḍayaḥ padmadevatābījamaṇḍalam 
rūpamityādikaṃ kiñcid dhyeyaṃ naiva kadācana // Dka_16

kuhakaṃ mantrajālaṃ ca prāṇāyāmādi dhāraṇam 
sarvametanna kartavyaṃ mokṣamakṣayamicchatā // Dka_17

nātra pūjā namaskāro na japo dhyānameva ca 
kevalaṃ jñānamityuktaṃ veditavyaṃ na kiñcana // Dka_18

bahirāhitacittānāṃ jāyante bandhahetavaḥ 
bahiścittaṃ nivāryaiva vindan loke na sīdati // Dka_19

nātra kiñcidbahirnāntaṃ na madhyaṃ nāpyadhaḥ kvacit 
sarvākāraṃ nirākāraṃ svasaṃvedyaṃ virājate // Dka_20

yadyadālokya yo jantuḥ kurute karmasañcayam 
tadgatirjāyate yasmān nirālokaṃ tu cintayet // Dka_21

heturnāsti phalaṃ nāsti nāsti karma svabhāvataḥ 
asadbhūtamidaṃ sarvaṃ nāsti loko na laukikaḥ // Dka_22

nirālambamidaṃ sarvaṃ nirālambaprakāśitam 
nirālambamidaṃ kṛtvā nirālambo bhaviṣyati // Dka_23

vyomākāraṃ mahāśūnyaṃ vyāpakaṃ yo na bhāvayet 
saṃsārī sa bhavelloke bījakośakrimiryathā // Dka_24

jñānotpattinimittaṃ tu kriyāścaryāḥ prakīrtitāḥ 
yogaṃ sālambanaṃ tyaktvā niṣprapañcaṃ vicintayet // Dka_25

pātālāt śaktiparyantaṃ sarvametadabhīpsitam 
bhagnaṃ yaiḥ śūnyamantreṇa te smṛtāḥ śūnyavedinaḥ // Dka_26

viṣaye lolupaṃ cittaṃ markaṭādapi cañcalam 
sarvaśūnyapade sthitvā tato nirvāṇameṣyati // Dka_27

sarvatattvādyasambhinnaṃ dehād bhinnaṃ tathaiva ca 
ahamasmādyasambhinnaṃ caitanyaṃ sarvatomukham // Dka_28

ākāśamiva sarvaṃ tu sabāhyābhyantaraṃ priye 
parānandamarūpaṃ tu paśyannānandabhāgbhavet // Dka_29

nirindhano yathā vahniḥ svayameva praśāmyati 
grāhyābhāvānmanastadvat svayameva pralīyate // Dka_30

mohikā mūrcchikā māyā svapnaśceti caturvidhaḥ 
suṣuptirjāgṛtiścaiva sarvametat parityajet // Dka_31

dehāt sūkṣmagatāt prāṇāc cittād buddherahaṅkṛteḥ 
sarvasmādbhinna evāhaṃ cintayan labhate citam // Dka_32

sadābhibhūtaye cittaṃ nidrayā smaraṇādinā 
bodhayitvā prayatnena kuryāt svasthaṃ punaḥ punaḥ // Dka_33

yadā sthiraṃ bhaveccittaṃ cālayanna kathaṃcana 
na kiñciccintayet tatra sthirameva tu kārayet // Dka_34

āśrayālambanaṃ cittaṃ tadvat kuryānnirāśrayam 
cañcalaṃ niścalaṃ kuryāt niścalaṃ na tu cālayet // Dka_35

sarvabhūtalaye jāte yadyadvyoma sunirmalam 
tattadrūpaṃ svakaṃ dhyāyed vyāptaṃ caiva tu nirmalam // Dka_36

tadeva janmasāphalyaṃ pāṇḍityamidameva hi 
caladvāyusamaṃ cittaṃ niścalaṃ dhriyate hi yat // Dka_37

naivordhvaṃ dhārayeccittaṃ na madhyaṃ nāpyadhaḥ kvacit 
antarbhāvavinirmuktaṃ sadā kuryānnirāśrayam // Dka_38

nidrāyāṃ bodhayeccittaṃ vikṣiptaṃ śamayet punaḥ 
pakṣadvayaparityāge samprāpte naiva cālayet // Dka_39

nirāśrayaṃ sadā cittaṃ sarvālambanavarjitam 
mano 'vasthāvinirmuktaṃ vijñeyaṃ muktilakṣaṇam // Dka_40

sarvālambanaśūnyaṃ ca dhārayitvā mano hṛdi 
yajjñānaṃ jāyate spaṣṭaṃ tadabhyāsaparo bhavet // Dka_41

ye dhyāyanti paraṃ śūnyaṃ niṣkalaṃ niravasthitam 
te yānti paramaṃ sthānaṃ janmamṛtyuvivarjitam // Dka_42

devā devyastathā cānye dharmādharmau ca tatphalam 
āśrayāśrayivijñānaṃ saṃsārasya ca bandhanam // Dka_43

āśrayo dvandvamityuktaṃ dvandvatyāgāt parodayaḥ 
jīvanmuktastadā yogī dehatyāgād vimucyate // Dka_44

vairāgyeṇa vapustyāgo na vai kāryo manīṣiṇā 
ārambhataḥ kriyānāśe svayameva vipatsyate // Dka_45

hṛtsaroje hyahaṃrūpā yā citirnirmalācalā 
ahaṅkāraparityāgāt sā citirmokṣadāyinī // Dka_46

sarvopādhivinirmuktaṃ cidrūpaṃ yannirantaram 
tacchivo 'hamiti dhyātvā sarvāsaktiṃ visarjayet // Dka_47

deśajātyādisambaddhān varṇāśramasamanvitān 
bhāvānetān parityajya svabhāvaṃ bhāvayedbudhaḥ // Dka_48

ahameko na me kaścin nāhamanyasya kasyacit 
na taṃ paśyāmi yasyāhaṃ taṃ na paśyāmi yo mama // Dka_49

ahameva paraṃ brahma jagannātho maheśvaraḥ 
iti syānniścito mukto baddhaḥ syādanyathā pumān // Dka_50

aśarīraṃ yadātmānaṃ paśyati jñānacakṣuṣā 
tadā bhavati śāntātmā sarvato vigataspṛhaḥ // Dka_51

yo 'sau sarveṣu śāstreṣu paṭhyate hyaja īśvaraḥ 
akāyo nirguṇo hyātmā so 'hamasmi na saṃśayaḥ // Dka_52

vijñāptimātro hi sadā viśuddhaḥ sarvatra yasmātsatataṃ vimuktaḥ 
nādeyaheyo hyahamapratarkyas tasmātsadā brahmamayo viśokaḥ // Dka_53

āmastakaṃ pādatalāvasānaṃ sāntarbahiścarmapaṭāvanaddham 
tatkṛtsnamevāmṛtarūpamanyac cidrūpamātmānamananyasiddhim // Dka_54

īśo 'hamevāsya carācarasya pitā ca mātā ca pitāmahaśca 
dhyānaṃ samāsthāya padaṃ caturthaṃ dhyāyanti māmeva vimuktikāmāḥ // Dka_55

brahmādibhirdevamanuṣyanāgair gandharvayakṣāpsarasāṃ gaṇaiśca 
yajñairanekairahameva pūjyo māmeva sarve pratipūjayanti // Dka_56

tapobhirugrairvividhaiśca dānair māmeva sarve pratipūjayanti 
bhūtāni cāhaṃ sthirajaṅgamāni yāvanti cānyānyahameva tāni // Dka_57

na sthūlasūkṣmo na ca śūnyarūpo jñānaikarūpo jagadekabandhuḥ 
nirantaro nirmala īśvaro 'haṃ svapnādyavasthācyutiniṣprapañcaḥ // Dka_58

anādivijñānamajaṃ purāṇaṃ guhāśayaṃ niṣkalamaprapañcam 
nirañjanaṃ niṣpratimaṃ nirīśam adṛśyamagrāhyamacintyarūpam // Dka_59

sanātanaṃ brahma nirantaraṃ yat pade pade so 'hamiti prapaśyet 
yo bhāvatastiṣṭhati niṣprakampaḥ sa brahmabhūto 'mṛtatāmupaiti // Dka_60

jñānamevaṃ varārohe kathitaṃ mokṣasiddhaye 
ācāraṃ kathyamānaṃ tu sāmprataṃ śṛṇu taṃ mayā // Dka_61

na snānaṃ na japaḥ pūjā homo naiva ca sādhanam 
agnikāryādikāryaṃ ca naitasyāsti maheśvari // Dka_62

niyamo 'pi na tasyāsti kṣetrapīṭhe ca sevanam 
nārcanaṃ pitṛkāryādi tīrthayātrā vratāni ca // Dka_63

dharmādharmaphalaṃ nāsti na tithirlaukikakriyā 
santyajetsarvakarmāṇi lokācāraṃ ca sarvaśaḥ // Dka_64

samayācāraniḥśeṣān kṛtyajātaṃ tu bandhanam 
saṃkalpaṃ ca vikalpaṃ ca ye cānye kuladharmikāḥ // Dka_65

siddhīśca vividhākārāḥ pātālādi rasāyanam 
pratyakṣeṇāpi labhyeran naiva gṛhṇīta sādhakaḥ // Dka_66

sarve te paśubandhāḥ syur adhomārgapradāyakāḥ 
etairnāsti parā muktiś cidrūpaṃ vyāpakaṃ vinā // Dka_67

yena kena viśeṣeṇa sarvāvastho 'pi yogadhṛk 
kṣetrapīṭhe ca sandehād varjayedyadi kautukam // Dka_68

kṛmikīṭapataṅgāśca tathā devi vanaspatīn 
na nāśayed budho jīvān paramārthamatiryataḥ // Dka_69

na mūlotpāṭanaṃ kuryāt pattracchedaṃ vivarjayet 
bhūtapīḍāṃ na kurvīta puṣpāṇāṃ ca nikṛntanam // Dka_70

svayaṃpatitapuṣpaistu kartavyaṃ śivapūjanam 
māraṇoccāṭanādīni vidveṣastambhane tathā // Dka_71

jvarabhūtagrahāveśavaśyākarṣaṇamohanam 
na kuryāt kṣudrakarmāṇi kāṣṭhapāṣāṇapūjanam // Dka_72

samo 'mitre ca mitre ca samo loṣṭe ca kāñcane 
abhilāṣo na kartavya indriyārthe kadācana // Dka_73

ātmārāmo bhavedyogī nirbhayo vigataspṛhaḥ 
samanindāpraśaṃsaśca sarvabhūtasamastathā // Dka_74

samadṛṣṭistu kartavyā yathātmani tathā pare 
vivādaṃ lokagoṣṭhīṃ ca kalahāśca vivarjayet // Dka_75
śāstragoṣṭhīṃ na kurvīta kubhāṣitasubhāṣitān // Dka_76

īrṣyāṃ paiśunyadambhe ca rāgaṃ mātsaryameva ca 
kāmakrodhau bhayaṃ śokaṃ tyajetsarvaṃ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ // Dka_77

sarvadvandvavinirmuktaḥ santataṃ janavarjitaḥ 
anenaiva śarīreṇa sarvajñaḥ san prakāśate // Dka_78

jñānenaiva yathā mokṣas tathā siddhirnirarthikā 
tathāpi bhogamicchantaḥ siddhimicchanti sādhakāḥ // Dka_79

aṇimādiguṇāvāptir jāyatāṃ vā na jāyatām 
tathāpi mucyate dehī patiṃ vijñāya nirmalam // Dka_80

pañcabhūtātmako dehaḥ śivastatraiva tiṣṭhati 
śivādyavaniparyanto loko 'yaṃ śaṅkarātmakaḥ // Dka_81

īdṛśaṃ jñāninaṃ dṛṣṭvā pūjayanti ca ye narāḥ 
gandhaṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ dhūpaṃ snānaṃ vastraṃ ca bhojanam // Dka_82

nivedayanti ye kecid vāṅmanaḥkāyakarmabhiḥ 
tathaiva te vimucyante muktimārgābhikāṅkṣiṇaḥ // Dka_83

stutinindākarāstasya puṇyapāpe samāpnuyuḥ 
yajjñānācaraṇaṃ pṛṣṭaṃ tat sarvaṃ kathitaṃ mayā 
kālajñānaṃ varārohe kimanyat paripṛcchasi // Dka_84
iti devīkālottarāgamaḥ parisamāptaḥ

TEXT WITH PADA MARKERS
translation: Devīkālottarāgama — 'The Āgama of the Goddess [entitled] Kālottara', i.e., the higher teaching of Goddess Kālī.

sanskrit:
sarveṣāmapi muktyarthaṃ muktimārgasya darśanam 
deveśa jñānamācāraṃ kṛpayā kathayasva me // Dka_1

jñānācārau varārohe kathayāmi tavādhunā 
praviśanti yato mokṣaṃ jñānino dhvastakalmaṣam // Dka_2
translation: O Lord of the gods, graciously teach me, for the sake of the liberation of all beings, the vision of the path of liberation — the knowledge and the conduct.

sanskrit:
yeṣāṃ bodhena saṃjātaṃ kālajñānaṃ varānane 
na teṣāṃ jāyate bodhaḥ śāstrakoṭiśatairapi // Dka_3
translation: O fair-hipped one, I shall now declare to you the knowledge and the conduct, through which the wise, their defilements destroyed, enter liberation.

sanskrit:
ato hi nirbhayo vidvān niḥśaṅko vigataspṛhaḥ 
jñānotsāhaparo bhūyāt śraddaddhāno nirākulaḥ // Dka_4
translation: O fair-faced one, for those in whom the knowledge of Kāla (Time) has arisen through awakening, no awakening arises even from hundreds of millions of scriptures.

sanskrit:
nirmamaḥ karuṇopetaḥ sarvabhūtābhayapradaḥ 
bhajet kālottaraṃ devi mumukṣuryogatatparaḥ // Dka_5
translation: Therefore the learned one should be fearless, free of doubt, free of longing, intent upon the ardour of knowledge, full of faith, and unperturbed.

sanskrit:
sa brahmā sa śivo viṣṇuḥ sa indraḥ sa ṣaḍānanaḥ 
sa guruḥ sarvadevāśca sa yogī sa tapodhanaḥ // Dka_6
translation: Free of possessiveness, endowed with compassion, granting safety to all beings, the seeker of liberation, devoted to yoga, should attend to the Kālottara, O Goddess.

sanskrit:
paṇḍitaḥ sa mahābhāgaḥ kṛtārthaḥ paramārthataḥ 
caladvāyusamaṃ cittaṃ dhriyate yena niścalam // Dka_7
translation: He is Brahmā, he is Śiva, he is Viṣṇu; he is Indra, he is the six-faced [Skanda]; he is the guru and all the gods; he is the yogin; he is the one whose wealth is austerity.

sanskrit:
sa upāyo mimokṣasya sadupāttaguṇastu saḥ 
sā prajñā tadiha sthairyaṃ tatpuṇyaṃ vyavasāyinām // Dka_8
translation: He is the true scholar, the highly blessed one, fulfilled in the highest sense — he by whom the mind, [otherwise] like moving wind, is held motionless.

sanskrit:
tadeva tīrthaṃ dānaṃ ca sa tapaśca na saṃśayaḥ 
yenopāyena badhyeta vāyubhiścalanaṃ manaḥ // Dka_9
translation: This is the means of liberation, and he is one possessed of good qualities. This is wisdom; this, here, is steadiness; this is the merit of the resolute.

sanskrit:
citte calati saṃsāro niścalo mokṣa eva tu 
tasmāccittaṃ sthiraṃ kuryāt prajñayā parayā budhaḥ // Dka_10
translation: That alone is the sacred ford, the gift, and the austerity — of this there is no doubt — namely the means by which the mind, which stirs with the winds, is held in check.

sanskrit:
ekāntikaṃ sukhaṃ yatra tathāivātyantikaṃ bhavet 
niṣkarmaṇi pare tattve ko na rajyeta paṇḍitaḥ // Dka_11
translation: When the mind stirs, there is saṃsāra; when it is motionless, there is liberation itself. Therefore the wise one should render the mind steadfast through supreme wisdom.

sanskrit:
nivṛtto viṣayajñānāt niṣkalajñānatatparaḥ 
anicchannapi medhāvī labhate mokṣamakṣayam // Dka_12
translation: Where there is bliss single-pointed and utterly final — in the supreme Reality beyond all activity — what wise person would not delight there?

sanskrit:
asmitākalayā yuktaṃ caitanyaṃ sakalaṃ smṛtam 
asmitārahitaṃ cetaś caitanyaṃ śaktirucyate // Dka_13
translation: Withdrawn from the cognition of sense-objects, intent on the knowledge of the partless, the discerning one obtains imperishable liberation even without desiring it.

sanskrit:
tathā prakāśitaṃ viśvaṃ śaktidhyānamudāhṛtam 
sarvālambavinirmuktaṃ niṣkalaṃ jñānamucyate // Dka_14
translation: Consciousness joined with the fragment of egoity is declared 'qualified' (sakala); consciousness free of egoity, however, is called śakti.

sanskrit:
ahamaṃśena yacchūnyaṃ cinmātrālokamadvayam 
muktibījaṃ tadākhyātaṃ parayogapravartakam // Dka_15
translation: And so the world, as it shines forth, is declared to be the contemplation of śakti; knowledge released from every support is called the partless (niṣkala).

sanskrit:
cakrāṇi nāḍayaḥ padmadevatābījamaṇḍalam 
rūpamityādikaṃ kiñcid dhyeyaṃ naiva kadācana // Dka_16
translation: That which is empty of the 'I'-fraction — consisting of consciousness alone, luminous, non-dual — is proclaimed the seed of liberation, the impeller of the supreme yoga.

sanskrit:
kuhakaṃ mantrajālaṃ ca prāṇāyāmādi dhāraṇam 
sarvametanna kartavyaṃ mokṣamakṣayamicchatā // Dka_17
translation: Wheels, channels, lotuses, deities, seed-syllables, the maṇḍala, visual forms — nothing of this sort is ever to be meditated upon.

sanskrit:
nātra pūjā namaskāro na japo dhyānameva ca 
kevalaṃ jñānamityuktaṃ veditavyaṃ na kiñcana // Dka_18
translation: Trickery, the web of mantras, breath-control and the like, and retention — none of this is to be done by one who desires imperishable liberation.

sanskrit:
bahirāhitacittānāṃ jāyante bandhahetavaḥ 
bahiścittaṃ nivāryaiva vindan loke na sīdati // Dka_19
translation: In this there is no worship, no prostration, no muttering, no meditation. Only knowledge, it is declared — nothing else is to be known.

sanskrit:
nātra kiñcidbahirnāntaṃ na madhyaṃ nāpyadhaḥ kvacit 
sarvākāraṃ nirākāraṃ svasaṃvedyaṃ virājate // Dka_20
translation: For those who have set their minds outward, the causes of bondage arise. Having checked the outward-turning mind, one does not sink in the world.

sanskrit:
yadyadālokya yo jantuḥ kurute karmasañcayam 
tadgatirjāyate yasmān nirālokaṃ tu cintayet // Dka_21
translation: Here there is nothing outer, nothing inner, no middle, nowhere anything below; formless yet possessing all forms, self-apprehended, it shines forth.

sanskrit:
heturnāsti phalaṃ nāsti nāsti karma svabhāvataḥ 
asadbhūtamidaṃ sarvaṃ nāsti loko na laukikaḥ // Dka_22
translation: Whatever a creature looks upon and thereby piles up a store of karma, from that his destiny is born. Therefore he should contemplate the lightless (nirāloka).

sanskrit:
nirālambamidaṃ sarvaṃ nirālambaprakāśitam 
nirālambamidaṃ kṛtvā nirālambo bhaviṣyati // Dka_23
translation: There is no cause, no result, no karma in its own nature. All this is of unreal being: there is no world, and nothing worldly.

sanskrit:
vyomākāraṃ mahāśūnyaṃ vyāpakaṃ yo na bhāvayet 
saṃsārī sa bhavelloke bījakośakrimiryathā // Dka_24
translation: All this is supportless, illumined by the supportless. Having made this supportless, one becomes supportless oneself.

sanskrit:
jñānotpattinimittaṃ tu kriyāścaryāḥ prakīrtitāḥ 
yogaṃ sālambanaṃ tyaktvā niṣprapañcaṃ vicintayet // Dka_25
translation: He who does not contemplate the sky-formed, the great Void, the all-pervading — he remains a wanderer in saṃsāra, like a worm inside a seed-pod.

sanskrit:
pātālāt śaktiparyantaṃ sarvametadabhīpsitam 
bhagnaṃ yaiḥ śūnyamantreṇa te smṛtāḥ śūnyavedinaḥ // Dka_26
translation: The astonishing rites are proclaimed only as an occasion for the arising of knowledge. Forsaking yoga that rests on supports, one should contemplate that which is free of all proliferation.

sanskrit:
viṣaye lolupaṃ cittaṃ markaṭādapi cañcalam 
sarvaśūnyapade sthitvā tato nirvāṇameṣyati // Dka_27
translation: Everything from the nether world up to śakti is [merely] an object of craving. Those by whom it is shattered by means of the emptiness-mantra are called 'knowers of the void'.

sanskrit:
sarvatattvādyasambhinnaṃ dehād bhinnaṃ tathaiva ca 
ahamasmādyasambhinnaṃ caitanyaṃ sarvatomukham // Dka_28
translation: The mind that lusts after sense-objects is more restless than a monkey. Stationed in the state of universal emptiness, it will then attain nirvāṇa.

sanskrit:
ākāśamiva sarvaṃ tu sabāhyābhyantaraṃ priye 
parānandamarūpaṃ tu paśyannānandabhāgbhavet // Dka_29
translation: Undivided from the very first of all principles, and likewise distinct from the body — undivided from the sense of 'I' — consciousness faces in all directions.

sanskrit:
nirindhano yathā vahniḥ svayameva praśāmyati 
grāhyābhāvānmanastadvat svayameva pralīyate // Dka_30
translation: All this, outer and inner alike, is like space, O beloved. Seeing the supreme bliss that is formless, one becomes a partaker of bliss.

sanskrit:
mohikā mūrcchikā māyā svapnaśceti caturvidhaḥ 
suṣuptirjāgṛtiścaiva sarvametat parityajet // Dka_31
translation: As a fire without fuel subsides of itself, so the mind, for lack of any object to seize, melts away of its own accord.

sanskrit:
dehāt sūkṣmagatāt prāṇāc cittād buddherahaṅkṛteḥ 
sarvasmādbhinna evāhaṃ cintayan labhate citam // Dka_32
translation: The bewitching, the stupefying, māyā, and dream — this fourfold — and deep sleep and waking as well: all of this one should abandon.

sanskrit:
sadābhibhūtaye cittaṃ nidrayā smaraṇādinā 
bodhayitvā prayatnena kuryāt svasthaṃ punaḥ punaḥ // Dka_33
translation: Reflecting 'I am distinct from all' — from the body, from that which moves in the subtle, from the vital breath, from the mind, from the intellect, from egoity — one obtains consciousness.

sanskrit:
yadā sthiraṃ bhaveccittaṃ cālayanna kathaṃcana 
na kiñciccintayet tatra sthirameva tu kārayet // Dka_34
translation: The mind is perpetually overpowered by sleep, by recollection, and the like. Rousing it with effort, one should restore it to itself, again and again.

sanskrit:
āśrayālambanaṃ cittaṃ tadvat kuryānnirāśrayam 
cañcalaṃ niścalaṃ kuryāt niścalaṃ na tu cālayet // Dka_35
translation: When the mind has become steady and cannot be moved in any way, one should think nothing there — one should simply keep it still.

sanskrit:
sarvabhūtalaye jāte yadyadvyoma sunirmalam 
tattadrūpaṃ svakaṃ dhyāyed vyāptaṃ caiva tu nirmalam // Dka_36
translation: The mind, which leans on a base and a support, one should render supportless; the restless one one should make still — and the still one one must not stir.

sanskrit:
tadeva janmasāphalyaṃ pāṇḍityamidameva hi 
caladvāyusamaṃ cittaṃ niścalaṃ dhriyate hi yat // Dka_37
translation: When the dissolution of all elements has come about, whatever purest expanse remains — that one should meditate upon as one's own form: all-pervading and immaculate.

sanskrit:
naivordhvaṃ dhārayeccittaṃ na madhyaṃ nāpyadhaḥ kvacit 
antarbhāvavinirmuktaṃ sadā kuryānnirāśrayam // Dka_38
translation: That alone is the fruition of birth; this alone is learning: that the mind, [otherwise] like moving wind, is held motionless.

sanskrit:
nidrāyāṃ bodhayeccittaṃ vikṣiptaṃ śamayet punaḥ 
pakṣadvayaparityāge samprāpte naiva cālayet // Dka_39
translation: One should not hold the mind upward, nor in the middle, nor downward anywhere; released from all inwardness, one should keep it forever unsupported.

sanskrit:
nirāśrayaṃ sadā cittaṃ sarvālambanavarjitam 
mano 'vasthāvinirmuktaṃ vijñeyaṃ muktilakṣaṇam // Dka_40
translation: From sleep one should wake the mind; when scattered, one should calm it again. When the abandonment of both wings is accomplished, one should not stir it at all.

sanskrit:
sarvālambanaśūnyaṃ ca dhārayitvā mano hṛdi 
yajjñānaṃ jāyate spaṣṭaṃ tadabhyāsaparo bhavet // Dka_41
translation: The mind ever unsupported, stripped of every support, freed from the mind's own conditions — this is to be recognized as the mark of liberation.

sanskrit:
ye dhyāyanti paraṃ śūnyaṃ niṣkalaṃ niravasthitam 
te yānti paramaṃ sthānaṃ janmamṛtyuvivarjitam // Dka_42
translation: Holding the mind in the heart, void of every support, whatever clear knowledge arises — to that one should devote one's practice.

sanskrit:
devā devyastathā cānye dharmādharmau ca tatphalam 
āśrayāśrayivijñānaṃ saṃsārasya ca bandhanam // Dka_43
translation: Those who meditate on the supreme Void — partless, without station — they pass to the supreme abode, which is free of birth and death.

sanskrit:
āśrayo dvandvamityuktaṃ dvandvatyāgāt parodayaḥ 
jīvanmuktastadā yogī dehatyāgād vimucyate // Dka_44
translation: Gods and goddesses and the rest, merit and demerit and their fruits — the cognition of a support and of what rests upon it: this is the bondage of saṃsāra.

sanskrit:
vairāgyeṇa vapustyāgo na vai kāryo manīṣiṇā 
ārambhataḥ kriyānāśe svayameva vipatsyate // Dka_45
translation: The 'support' is declared to be the pair of opposites; from the renunciation of the pairs the Highest arises. The yogin is then liberated while living, and at the body's fall he is released.

sanskrit:
hṛtsaroje hyahaṃrūpā yā citirnirmalācalā 
ahaṅkāraparityāgāt sā citirmokṣadāyinī // Dka_46
translation: The sage should not cast off the body through [forced] aversion; when activity is undone at its very root, [the body] will perish of itself.

sanskrit:
sarvopādhivinirmuktaṃ cidrūpaṃ yannirantaram 
tacchivo 'hamiti dhyātvā sarvāsaktiṃ visarjayet // Dka_47
translation: In the lotus of the heart, that consciousness (citi) which has the form of 'I' — pure and unmoving — upon the abandonment of egoity, that very consciousness bestows liberation.

sanskrit:
deśajātyādisambaddhān varṇāśramasamanvitān 
bhāvānetān parityajya svabhāvaṃ bhāvayedbudhaḥ // Dka_48
translation: Meditating 'I am that Śiva' upon that which is stripped of every limiting adjunct, whose nature is consciousness, and which is uninterrupted, one should cast off all attachment.

sanskrit:
ahameko na me kaścin nāhamanyasya kasyacit 
na taṃ paśyāmi yasyāhaṃ taṃ na paśyāmi yo mama // Dka_49
translation: Discarding those notions tied to place, birth, and the like — furnished as they are with class and station — the wise one should contemplate his own true nature.

sanskrit:
ahameva paraṃ brahma jagannātho maheśvaraḥ 
iti syānniścito mukto baddhaḥ syādanyathā pumān // Dka_50
translation: I am one alone: nothing is mine, and I am not another's. I do not behold him whose I am, nor do I behold him who is mine.

sanskrit:
aśarīraṃ yadātmānaṃ paśyati jñānacakṣuṣā 
tadā bhavati śāntātmā sarvato vigataspṛhaḥ // Dka_51
translation: 'I alone am the supreme Brahman, the Lord of the world, Maheśvara.' One who is resolved thus is liberated; otherwise a man remains bound.

sanskrit:
yo 'sau sarveṣu śāstreṣu paṭhyate hyaja īśvaraḥ 
akāyo nirguṇo hyātmā so 'hamasmi na saṃśayaḥ // Dka_52
translation: When one beholds the self as bodiless through the eye of knowledge, then one becomes a tranquil self, free of longing on every side.

sanskrit:
vijñāptimātro hi sadā viśuddhaḥ sarvatra yasmātsatataṃ vimuktaḥ 
nādeyaheyo hyahamapratarkyas tasmātsadā brahmamayo viśokaḥ // Dka_53
translation: That unborn Lord who is proclaimed in all the scriptures — the self, bodiless, devoid of qualities — 'I am he': of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit:
āmastakaṃ pādatalāvasānaṃ sāntarbahiścarmapaṭāvanaddham 
tatkṛtsnamevāmṛtarūpamanyac cidrūpamātmānamananyasiddhim // Dka_54
translation: I am indeed nothing but pure awareness — ever pure, and since I am everywhere, ever released: neither to be seized nor abandoned, beyond all reasoning. Therefore I am ever one with Brahman, without sorrow.

sanskrit:
īśo 'hamevāsya carācarasya pitā ca mātā ca pitāmahaśca 
dhyānaṃ samāsthāya padaṃ caturthaṃ dhyāyanti māmeva vimuktikāmāḥ // Dka_55
translation: From the crown of the head to the soles of the feet, wrapped within and without in a covering of skin — all that is but a mortal form [v.l. amṛtarūpam, 'of immortal form']; the other, the self whose form is consciousness, is the attainment of non-otherness.

sanskrit:
brahmādibhirdevamanuṣyanāgair gandharvayakṣāpsarasāṃ gaṇaiśca 
yajñairanekairahameva pūjyo māmeva sarve pratipūjayanti // Dka_56
translation: I alone am the Lord of all this, moving and motionless; I am the father, the mother, and the grandsire. Establishing themselves in meditation on the fourth state, those who long for release meditate on me alone.

sanskrit:
tapobhirugrairvividhaiśca dānair māmeva sarve pratipūjayanti 
bhūtāni cāhaṃ sthirajaṅgamāni yāvanti cānyānyahameva tāni // Dka_57
translation: By Brahmā and the others — gods, men, and serpents, and the hosts of gandharvas, yakṣas, and apsarases — and through countless sacrifices, I alone am to be worshipped: all of them worship only me.

sanskrit:
na sthūlasūkṣmo na ca śūnyarūpo jñānaikarūpo jagadekabandhuḥ 
nirantaro nirmala īśvaro 'haṃ svapnādyavasthācyutiniṣprapañcaḥ // Dka_58
translation: Through fierce austerities and manifold donations all of them worship only me. And I am the beings, the stationary and the moving; whatever else exists — I myself am that.

sanskrit:
anādivijñānamajaṃ purāṇaṃ guhāśayaṃ niṣkalamaprapañcam 
nirañjanaṃ niṣpratimaṃ nirīśam adṛśyamagrāhyamacintyarūpam // Dka_59
translation: I am neither gross nor subtle, nor have I the form of the void; my form is knowledge alone, the one kin of the world. I am the Lord — uninterrupted, immaculate, never fallen into states such as dreaming, free of all proliferation.

sanskrit:
sanātanaṃ brahma nirantaraṃ yat pade pade so 'hamiti prapaśyet 
yo bhāvatastiṣṭhati niṣprakampaḥ sa brahmabhūto 'mṛtatāmupaiti // Dka_60
translation: Beginningless awareness, unborn, ancient, dwelling in the cavern, partless, free of proliferation, without stain, without likeness, without overlord — invisible, ungraspable, of inconceivable form.

sanskrit:
jñānamevaṃ varārohe kathitaṃ mokṣasiddhaye 
ācāraṃ kathyamānaṃ tu sāmprataṃ śṛṇu taṃ mayā // Dka_61
translation: The eternal, uninterrupted Brahman one should behold at every step, thinking 'I am he.' He who stands in that state utterly without tremor becomes Brahman and attains immortality.

sanskrit:
na snānaṃ na japaḥ pūjā homo naiva ca sādhanam 
agnikāryādikāryaṃ ca naitasyāsti maheśvari // Dka_62
translation: Thus, O fair-hipped one, has knowledge been taught for the winning of liberation. Now listen as I declare the conduct (ācāra).

sanskrit:
niyamo 'pi na tasyāsti kṣetrapīṭhe ca sevanam 
nārcanaṃ pitṛkāryādi tīrthayātrā vratāni ca // Dka_63
translation: For this one, O Maheśvarī, there is no bathing, no muttering, no worship, no oblation, no ritual practice — no fire-rites nor any other duty.

sanskrit:
dharmādharmaphalaṃ nāsti na tithirlaukikakriyā 
santyajetsarvakarmāṇi lokācāraṃ ca sarvaśaḥ // Dka_64
translation: He has no fixed rule either, nor attendance upon sacred fields and seats (kṣetra and pīṭha), no image-worship, no ancestral rites, no pilgrimages to holy fords, no vows.

sanskrit:
samayācāraniḥśeṣān kṛtyajātaṃ tu bandhanam 
saṃkalpaṃ ca vikalpaṃ ca ye cānye kuladharmikāḥ // Dka_65
translation: There is no fruit of merit or demerit, no lunar day, no worldly rite. One should renounce all actions and every worldly convention without remainder.

sanskrit:
siddhīśca vividhākārāḥ pātālādi rasāyanam 
pratyakṣeṇāpi labhyeran naiva gṛhṇīta sādhakaḥ // Dka_66
translation: All the class of ritual acts — the observances of the samaya without exception — is bondage; so too are intention and deliberation, and whatever other Kaula duties there are.

sanskrit:
sarve te paśubandhāḥ syur adhomārgapradāyakāḥ 
etairnāsti parā muktiś cidrūpaṃ vyāpakaṃ vinā // Dka_67
translation: And the siddhis of every kind — the alchemical [elixirs] beginning with Pātāla — even if they were gained before one's very eyes, the sādhaka should never take them up.

sanskrit:
yena kena viśeṣeṇa sarvāvastho 'pi yogadhṛk 
kṣetrapīṭhe ca sandehād varjayedyadi kautukam // Dka_68
translation: All of these would be bonds of the bound soul (paśu), leading along the downward path. Through them there is no supreme liberation — [there is none] apart from the all-pervading one whose form is consciousness.

sanskrit:
kṛmikīṭapataṅgāśca tathā devi vanaspatīn 
na nāśayed budho jīvān paramārthamatiryataḥ // Dka_69
translation: Whatever the particular means, even the bearer of yoga in every state should, out of scruple, avoid the [enticements of] field and seat, should any longing arise. [Text uncertain.]

sanskrit:
na mūlotpāṭanaṃ kuryāt pattracchedaṃ vivarjayet 
bhūtapīḍāṃ na kurvīta puṣpāṇāṃ ca nikṛntanam // Dka_70
translation: Worms, insects, and moths, and likewise, O Goddess, the trees — the wise one should destroy no living being, for his mind is set upon the highest good.

sanskrit:
svayaṃpatitapuṣpaistu kartavyaṃ śivapūjanam 
māraṇoccāṭanādīni vidveṣastambhane tathā // Dka_71
translation: He should not tear [plants] up by the root, nor cut off their leaves; he should inflict no pain on living beings, nor sever flowers.

sanskrit:
jvarabhūtagrahāveśavaśyākarṣaṇamohanam 
na kuryāt kṣudrakarmāṇi kāṣṭhapāṣāṇapūjanam // Dka_72
translation: The worship of Śiva is to be performed with flowers that have fallen of themselves. Slaying, driving away, and the like — and likewise hostile rites and immobilizing spells — [these he must not practise].

sanskrit:
samo 'mitre ca mitre ca samo loṣṭe ca kāñcane 
abhilāṣo na kartavya indriyārthe kadācana // Dka_73
translation: Fever-magic, seizure by spirits, possession (āveśa), subjugation, attraction, and bewitchment — he should not work these petty rites, nor worship wood and stone.

sanskrit:
ātmārāmo bhavedyogī nirbhayo vigataspṛhaḥ 
samanindāpraśaṃsaśca sarvabhūtasamastathā // Dka_74
translation: Equal toward enemy and friend, equal toward a clod and gold — he should never form desire for the objects of the senses.

sanskrit:
samadṛṣṭistu kartavyā yathātmani tathā pare 
vivādaṃ lokagoṣṭhīṃ ca kalahāśca vivarjayet // Dka_75
translation: The yogin should take his delight in the Self, fearless and free of craving, unmoved by blame and praise alike, and equal toward all beings.

sanskrit: śāstragoṣṭhīṃ na kurvīta kubhāṣitasubhāṣitān // Dka_76
translation: He should maintain an equal gaze — toward others as toward himself. And he should shun contention, worldly chatter, and strife.

sanskrit:
īrṣyāṃ paiśunyadambhe ca rāgaṃ mātsaryameva ca 
kāmakrodhau bhayaṃ śokaṃ tyajetsarvaṃ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ // Dka_77
translation: He should not hold discourse on the scriptures — neither ill-spoken nor well-spoken words.

sanskrit:
sarvadvandvavinirmuktaḥ santataṃ janavarjitaḥ 
anenaiva śarīreṇa sarvajñaḥ san prakāśate // Dka_78
translation: Envy, malice, and deceit, attachment and jealousy; lust and wrath, fear and grief — all of these he should renounce, gradually, gradually.

sanskrit:
jñānenaiva yathā mokṣas tathā siddhirnirarthikā 
tathāpi bhogamicchantaḥ siddhimicchanti sādhakāḥ // Dka_79
translation: Released from every pair of opposites, ever shunning the company of men, he shines forth — omniscient — in this very body.

sanskrit:
aṇimādiguṇāvāptir jāyatāṃ vā na jāyatām 
tathāpi mucyate dehī patiṃ vijñāya nirmalam // Dka_80
translation: Just as liberation comes through knowledge alone, so any [other] accomplishment (siddhi) is worthless; yet it is because they crave enjoyment that sādhakas hanker after siddhi.

sanskrit:
pañcabhūtātmako dehaḥ śivastatraiva tiṣṭhati 
śivādyavaniparyanto loko 'yaṃ śaṅkarātmakaḥ // Dka_81
translation: Whether the attainment of the lordly powers — aṇimā and the rest — comes about or not, the embodied one is released all the same, once he has known the immaculate Lord.

sanskrit:
īdṛśaṃ jñāninaṃ dṛṣṭvā pūjayanti ca ye narāḥ 
gandhaṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ dhūpaṃ snānaṃ vastraṃ ca bhojanam // Dka_82
translation: The body is composed of the five elements, and Śiva abides in that very body. This whole world, from Śiva down to the earth, is of the nature of Śaṅkara.

sanskrit:
nivedayanti ye kecid vāṅmanaḥkāyakarmabhiḥ 
tathaiva te vimucyante muktimārgābhikāṅkṣiṇaḥ // Dka_83
translation: And those men who, beholding such a knower, honour him — with fragrance, flowers, fruit, incense, [water for] bathing, garments, and food — ...

sanskrit:
stutinindākarāstasya puṇyapāpe samāpnuyuḥ 
yajjñānācaraṇaṃ pṛṣṭaṃ tat sarvaṃ kathitaṃ mayā 
kālajñānaṃ varārohe kimanyat paripṛcchasi // Dka_84
translation: whatever they offer through the deeds of speech, mind, and body — they, longing as they do for the path of liberation, are in like manner set free.

sanskrit: iti devīkālottarāgamaḥ parisamāptaḥ
translation: Those who praise him or blame him would reap the merit and the sin [thereof]. That knowledge and conduct which was asked — all of it has been told by me. The knowledge of Kāla, O fair-hipped one: what else would you ask?

sanskrit: Devīkālottarāgama

sarveṣāmapi muktyarthaṃ muktimārgasya darśanam 
deveśa jñānamācāraṃ kṛpayā kathayasva me // Dka_1
